newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses down again, mark stronger still.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses down again, mark stronger still.

text.p: Leading European bourses weakened in early trading on Thursday after Wall Street's third loss in a row overnight.

On the currency markets, the mark's gradual recovery against the dollar this week was bolstered by official comments indicating the Bundesbank council, which was meeting on Thursday, would not cut German interest rates again.
Leading London stocks were trading lower despite a boost to the value of chemicals giant ICI, which gained after its third-quarter profits, while lower, contained no new shocks for the stock market.

Dealers said despite the weak performance in New York -- where the Dow ended 25.34 points lower at 6,036.46 after being down nearly 70 points at one time -- the market was underpinned by steady gilts and a firm overnight performance from Treasuries.
ICI dominated early dealing, confounding market expectations with a 17-1/2 pence rise to 793 after the group announced third-quarter results at the lower end of forecasts.

"ICI aside, the rest of the market is not looking so bright and I can't see this one stock pulling the entire market up," one trader said, noting that gainers and losers were roughly balanced and trading appeared quiet.

German shares, which were stronger in pre-bourse electronic trade, opened bourse trading half a percent down. But dealers said they saw the market stable or recovering from the tumble taken on Wednesday by software group SAP AG after a profits warning.
Frankfurt traders said they would be keeping a keen eye on the U.S. market and the bourse could post further losses if Wall Street traded weaker again on Thursday.
French shares started lower and turned mixed in line with futures contracts on profit-taking on the last day of the October account. The main CAC-40 index was flat.

The dollar opened softer in Europe as the mark's recovery this week was boosted not only by the fading of German interest rate cut expectations but also by a surprise cut in the Italian discount rate late on Wednesday.

Lingering speculation of a cut in German rates at the regular Thursday Bundesbank meeting was dashed on Wednesday by the central bank's chief economist, Otmar Issing, and its vice-president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum.

Issing said key German rates were at historic lows and nothing more should be expected or was necessary. Gaddum said current interest rate levels were correct and the central bank wanted to keep rates steady for as long as possible.
The dollar was trading at 1.5195 marks compared with 1.5225 late on Wednesday. Chartists predicted there would be strong support for the dollar at 1.5180.
Against the yen, the dollar was at 112.63 compared with 113.05 late Wednesday.

Meanwhile, Sweden's Riksbank (central bank) cut its deposit and lending rates by half a percentage point and its key repo rate by a quarter of a percentage point. The Swedish crown eased slightly in reaction to 4.3315 to the mark from 4.3200 earlier.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5195 marks and 112.63 yen compared with 1.5225 and 113.05 yen on Wednesday.
STOCKS AT 0900 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 4.6 at 4023.8
Germany's DAX index was down 15.18 at 2684.35.
The Paris CAC-40 index was flat at 2,148.8.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $383.70 an ounce in the morning, compared with $383.55 at the close in London on Wednesday. Silver was also firmer at $4.99.
